dervis-irab:1-19.t:
* I'rab:
(وَالْمُرْسَلاتِ عُرْفاً) Abū Ḥayyān said in al-Nahr: «This sūra is Meccan, and its connection with what precedes it is very clear: He mentioned that He, the Exalted, has mercy on whom He wills and punishes the wrongdoers, and this is a true promise from Him; so He swore to its occurrence and said إن ما توعدون لواقع. And since the things sworn by are qualified nouns that have been omitted, their attributes being put in their place, there arose disagreement about those qualified nouns. What appears is that the things sworn by are two, and for this reason the conjunction came with the wāw in والناشرات, and conjunction with the wāw signals difference; whereas conjunction with the fāʾ, when it is among attributes, indicates that they go back to a single qualified noun. Once this is established, the apparent meaning is that He swore first by the winds, which is indicated by the conjunction of the attribute with the fāʾ; and the second oath contains an ascent to something nobler than the first thing sworn by, namely the angels; and His saying فالفارقات فالملقيات is among their attributes, and their casting of the Reminder, which is what Allah the Exalted sent down, is properly attributed to them. And what is mentioned of the exegetes' disagreement about what is meant by these attributes should be taken as illustration, not specification. The answer to the oath and what is conjoined to it is إن ما توعدون; ما is a relative noun meaning الذي, and the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. إن الذي توعدونه; it is the noun of إنّ, and His saying لواقع is its khabar (predicate).» We have prefaced with this useful glimpse to clarify the truth and to ward off the confusion that may arise from the exegetes' disagreement, and after it we return to the parsing. The wāw is for the oath; المرسلات is genitive (majrūr) by the wāw of the oath, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb, implied as «I swear». As for عرفا, either it is from ʿurf al-faras (with ḍamma on the ʿayn), i.e. the hair of a horse's neck, in which case it is parsed as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun concealed in المرسلات, the meaning being by way of simile, i.e. in the state of being ʿurf, i.e. resembling a horse's mane in their succession and following one another as it does; or it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), as if He said: by those sent forth in a sending, i.e. in succession. Or it is from al-ʿurf, which is kindness (al-maʿrūf), in the manner of the saying of al-Ḥuṭayʾa:
من يفعل الخير لا يعدم جوازيه ... لا يذهب العرف بين الله والناس
(Whoever does good will not lack its recompense; kindness is not lost between Allah and people.)
And it is accusative (manṣūb) as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. they were sent for beneficence and kindness, or accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ). (فَالْعاصِفاتِ عَصْفاً) The fāʾ is a conjunction for immediate sequence; العاصفات is conjoined to المرسلات, and it is an active participle from al-ʿaṣf in the sense of intensity. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «The wind ʿaṣafat, ʿaṣfan, of the pattern of ḍaraba, and also ʿuṣūfan: it became violent.» And عصفا is an emphasizing maṣdar, so it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). (وَالنَّاشِراتِ نَشْراً فَالْفارِقاتِ فَرْقاً فَالْمُلْقِياتِ ذِكْراً) الناشرات is also conjoined, and نشرا is an absolute object; فالفارقات is also conjoined, and فرقا is an absolute object; فالملقيات is also conjoined, and ذكرا is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of الملقيات, i.e. of the angels who descend with the revelation to the prophets. (عُذْراً أَوْ نُذْراً) These are two maṣdars: from ʿadhara, when one effaces wrongdoing, and from andhara, when one warns against disbelief, like kufr and shukr. They are accusative as objects of purpose. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed them to be accusative as a badal (substitute) of ذكرا. And Abū al-Baqāʾ's wording:
«In عذرا أو نذرا there are two aspects. One: they are two maṣdars whose middle letter may be quiescent or take ḍamma. The second: they are plurals of ʿadhīr and nadhīr. On the first, they are accusative as objects of purpose or as a substitute of ذكرا; on the second, they are two ḥāls of the pronoun in الملقيات, i.e. excusing and warning.» (إِنَّما تُوعَدُونَ لَواقِعٌ) The clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to the oath. إنّ is a particle resembling the verb; ما is a relative noun, the noun of إنّ; the clause توعدون is the ṣila (relative clause); the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa) and واقع is the predicate of إنّ; the referent pronoun is omitted, i.e. إن الذي توعدونه. (فَإِذَا النُّجُومُ طُمِسَتْ) The fāʾ is resumptive; إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; النجوم is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of an omitted verb explained by what follows, and the clause طمست is explicative, with no grammatical position. On the apodosis (jawāb) of إذا there are two views. One is that it is omitted, its implied form being «when the stars are effaced, what you are promised will occur», as indicated by His saying إنما توعدون لواقع. The second is that it is لأي يوم أجلت, on the implication of a saying, i.e. «it will be said: for what day were they deferred?», so the verb (of saying) is in reality the apodosis. The meaning of طمست is: erased and obliterated, and their light gone. (وَإِذَا السَّماءُ فُرِجَتْ وَإِذَا الْجِبالُ نُسِفَتْ وَإِذَا الرُّسُلُ أُقِّتَتْ) Clauses conjoined to the clause فإذا النجوم طمست. The meaning of فرجت is: opened, so that it became gates. The meaning of نسفت is: crumbled like flowing sand, then the wind carries it away. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «The wind nasafat the dust, nasfan, of the pattern of ḍaraba: it uprooted it and scattered it.» The meaning of أقتت is وقتت, and it was read with both, i.e. gathered for a known time. Al-Zajjāj said: what is meant by this taʾqīt or tawqīt is the clarification of the time in which they will be brought to bear witness against their nations; and the wāw, when it takes a ḍamma, may be made a hamza. Al-Mubarrad said in his Kāmil: «Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: وإذا الرسل أقتت, and the origin is وقتت; were it outside the Qur'an, it would be permissible to make the wāw overt if you wished.» (لِأَيِّ يَوْمٍ أُجِّلَتْ، لِيَوْمِ الْفَصْلِ) لأي يوم is attached to أجلت, i.e. أجلت لأي يوم. The clause is the speech of an omitted saying, in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of the nominative of أقتت, i.e. «it being said: for what day were they deferred?»; or it has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of إذا, as has preceded. ليوم الفصل is a substitute of لأي يوم with repetition of the governing element; you may also attach it to an omitted verb, i.e. «they were deferred for the Day of Decision». (وَما أَدْراكَ ما يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause أدراك is its predicate, and the kāf is the first direct object. His saying ما يوم الفصل is a clause of a subject, namely the interrogative ما, and a predicate, namely يوم الفصل, standing in place of the second object of إدراك, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative. The first interrogative means deeming far-fetched and disapproval, and the second is for magnification and making terrible. (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) ويل is a subject; what licensed beginning with it is the sense of imprecation in it. Al-Zamakhsharī's wording: «If you say: how did the indefinite noun occur as a subject in His saying ويل يومئذ للمكذبين? I say: in its origin it is an accusative maṣdar standing in place of its verb, but it was diverted to the nominative to indicate the fixity and permanence of the meaning of destruction for those imprecated against; similar is سلام عليكم. ويلا in the accusative is permissible, but it was not read so.» يومئذ is an adverb annexed to its like, and it is attached to ويل or is an adjective of it; the nunation is a substitute for omitted clauses taken from the context, the implied form being «on the day when stars are effaced and what follows it occurs». للمكذبين is the predicate of ويل. (أَلَمْ نُهْلِكِ الْأَوَّلِينَ ثُمَّ نُتْبِعُهُمُ الْآخِرِينَ) The hamza is for the interrogative of affirmation (istifhām taqrīrī), because the interrogative is in origin one of disapproval, and it has entered upon a negation, and the negation of a negation is an affirmation, and this is expressed as the interrogative of affirmation. لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to past) and jussive; نهلك is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as «We»; الأولين is the direct object. ثم is a conjunction for sequence with delay; نتبعهم is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) as a resumption, i.e. «then We will make them followed»; and الآخرين is a second direct object. (كَذلِكَ نَفْعَلُ بِالْمُجْرِمِينَ، وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) كذلك is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. «like that hideous action We do»; بالمجرمين is attached to نفعل. The parsing of ويل يومئذ للمكذبين has preceded, and the secret of its repetition will come in the section on rhetoric.

* Rhetoric:
The verse «ويل يومئذ للمكذبين» is repeated in this sūra ten times, and the secret in it is the increase of intimidation. Repetition in the context of encouragement and intimidation is acceptable and fine, especially when the verses preceding the repeated occurrences differ, as here.

* Benefits:
It is not permissible to conjoin «نتبعهم» to «نهلك», because the conjunction would require that it be «We destroyed the former peoples», since لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to past) and jussive; so the meaning would be «then We made the later ones follow them in destruction», and the matter is not so, because the destruction of the later ones has not yet occurred.

dervis-irab:20-34.t:
* Vocabulary:
(فَقَدَرْنا) Without doubling, from al-qudra (power); and it was read with doubling, from al-taqdīr (measuring/ordaining). The first is indicated by فنعم القادرون. In al-Qurṭubī: «Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read فقدّرنا with doubling, and the rest read it light; they are two dialectal forms with the meaning of فقدرنا without doubling.» In al-Miṣbāḥ: «I qadartu the thing, qadran, of the patterns of ḍaraba and qatala, and qaddartuhu, taqdīran, with the same meaning; and the noun is al-qadar, with two fatḥas.» And his saying ﷺ فاقدروا له means: reckon the number of the month, so complete Shaʿbān as thirty days.
(كِفاتاً) Al-Jalāl said: «a maṣdar (verbal noun) of kafata in the sense of gathering together.» He said in al-Qāmūs:
«kafatahu, yakfituhu: he turned him away from his direction, so he was turned away; and the thing to himself: he gathered it and drew it in, like kaffatahu; and the bird and other things, kaftan, kifātan, kafītan and kafatānan: it sped in flying and running.» So is كفاتا the maṣdar of the transitive kafata in the sense of «gathered», or the maṣdar of the intransitive kafata of the bird?! The words of the author of al-Qāmūs are misleading. After that he said in al-Qāmūs: «And al-kifāt (with kasra) is the place in which a thing is gathered, i.e. drawn together and collected; and the earth is a kifāt for us.» Al-Zamakhsharī and Abū Ḥayyān followed this. The exegetes refuted al-Jalāl because kafata is of the pattern of ḍaraba; so the truth is that it is a noun of place. In al-Mukhtār: «kafatahu: he drew it to himself, of the pattern of ḍaraba; and al-kifāt (with kasra) is the place in which a thing is gathered, i.e. drawn together and collected; and the earth is a kifāt for us.» And al-Samīn's wording: «al-kifāt is a name for the container in which a thing is gathered, i.e. collected; one says kafatahu, yakfituhu, i.e. he collected it and drew it together», until he said: «and it is said كفاتا is a plural of kāfit, like ṣiyām and qiyām as plurals of ṣāʾim and qāʾim; and it is said rather that it is a maṣdar like al-kitāb and al-ḥisāb.» More of this exposition will come in the section on i'rab.
(كَالْقَصْرِ) [i.e. like the palace,] of buildings, in its hugeness and height.
(جِمالَتٌ) With kasra on the jīm, the plural of jamal (camel), and the tāʾ is for the feminine of the plural. One says jamal, jimāl and jimāla, like dhakar, dhikār and dhikāra, and ḥajar, ḥijār and ḥijāra. It is said that it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), like al-dhikāra and al-ḥijāra. And جمالات was read; it may be a plural of jimāla, or a plural of jimāl, so that it is a plural of a plural; and it may be a plural of jamal, as in the saying رجالات قريش. More of this exposition will come in the section on rhetoric.

* I'rab:
(أَلَمْ نَخْلُقْكُمْ مِنْ ماءٍ مَهِينٍ) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and affirmation; لم is a particle of negation, conversion (to past) and jussive; نخلقكم is an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir), implied as «We»; the kāf is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); من ماء is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) نخلقكم, and مهين is a naʿt (adjective) of ماء. The من of beginning is an indication that He, the Exalted, is able to originate, and whoever is able to originate is able to restore. (فَجَعَلْناهُ فِي قَرارٍ مَكِينٍ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; جعلناه is a verb, its agent and its direct object; في قرار is in the place of the second object, and مكين is an adjective of قرار, i.e. a place in which the semen is preserved from the harms that would spoil it, such as air; and the قرار is the womb. (إِلى قَدَرٍ مَعْلُومٍ) إلى قدر: the preposition and its genitive noun are in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. deferred to a known measure; معلوم is an adjective of قدر. (فَقَدَرْنا فَنِعْمَ الْقادِرُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; قدرنا is a verb and its agent; the fāʾ is a conjunction; نعم is an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing praise; القادرون is the agent, and the one specified for praise is omitted, i.e. «We». (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded. (أَلَمْ نَجْعَلِ الْأَرْضَ كِفاتاً أَحْياءً وَأَمْواتاً) The hamza is for the interrogative of disapproval and affirmation; لم is a particle of negation, conversion and jussive; نجعل is an imperfect verb, jussive by لم, its agent latent, implied as «We»; الأرض is the first direct object and كفاتا the second direct object of نجعل, because it is for transformation (taṣyīr). أحياء and أمواتا are accusative as two direct objects of كفاتا, if it is established that كفاتا is a maṣdar, or a plural of kāfit, since that is an active participle. If it is not a maṣdar but a noun of place, then their accusative is by an implied verb indicated by كفاتا, its implied form being «it gathers», the meaning being: it gathers the living on its back and the dead in its belly. Abū Ḥayyān's wording:
«أحياء and أمواتا are accusative by a verb indicated by what precedes, i.e. it gathers the living on its back and the dead in its belly.» And al-Zamakhsharī said: «It is possible that the meaning be: it gathers you living and dead, so that they are accusative as ḥāls of the pronoun, because it is known that it is the gathering-place of humankind.» (وَجَعَلْنا فِيها رَواسِيَ شامِخاتٍ وَأَسْقَيْناكُمْ ماءً فُراتاً) The wāw is a conjunction; جعلنا is a verb and its agent; فيها is attached to جعلنا if it means «We created», and is in the place of the second object if جعلنا means «We made (into)». رواسي is the object of جعلنا and شامخات an adjective of رواسي. أسقيناكم is conjoined to جعلنا; ماء is the second object and فراتا an adjective of ماء; al-furāt is sweet water. (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded. (انْطَلِقُوا إِلى ما كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ) The clause is the speech of an omitted, resumed saying. انطلقوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; إلى ما is attached to انطلقوا; the clause كنتم has no grammatical position because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما; كان and its noun; به is attached to تكذبون; the clause تكذبون is the khabar (predicate) of كنتم, and the referent pronoun is the pronoun in به. (انْطَلِقُوا إِلى ظِلٍّ ذِي ثَلاثِ شُعَبٍ) انطلقوا is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the first انطلقوا; إلى ظل is attached to انطلقوا, and ذي ثلاث شعب is an adjective of ظل. More of this meaning will come in the section on rhetoric. (لا ظَلِيلٍ وَلا يُغْنِي مِنَ اللَّهَبِ) لا is negative, and ظليل is a negated adjective, because shade is never anything but shading; so negating it of it indicates that He called it shade in mockery and derision of them. ولا يغني من اللهب is conjoined to the negated element; يغني is an imperfect verb whose agent is «it», the shade; من اللهب is attached to يغني; and the clause is in the position of the genitive, i.e. not availing them anything against the heat of the flame. (إِنَّها تَرْمِي بِشَرَرٍ كَالْقَصْرِ) The clause stands as a causal explanation of the non-availing of the non-shading shade. إنّ and its noun, the pronoun referring to Jahannam, because the talk is about it; the clause ترمي is the predicate of إنّ; بشرر is attached to ترمي. al-sharar is what flies off from it; you say: a fire with sharār and sharar, and a sharāra and a sharara flew off from it. كالقصر is an adjective of شرر, i.e. every spark is like a qaṣr, of palaces, in its hugeness. More of this simile will come in the section on rhetoric. (كَأَنَّهُ جِمالَتٌ صُفْرٌ) The clause is a second adjective of شرر; كأنّ and its noun; جمالة is its predicate and صفر an adjective of جمالة. (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying «أحياء وأمواتا» there is indefiniteness: He made them indefinite, although it gathers all the living and the dead, for magnification, as if it were said: living ones beyond counting and dead ones beyond reckoning; besides which, the living and dead of humankind are not all the living and the dead.
2- And He made رواسي شامخات and ماء فراتا indefinite to convey partition, because in the sky there are mountains — Allah the Exalted said: «وينزل من السماء من جبال فيها من برد» — and in it there is much sweet water; indeed it is its source and its outflow.
3- In His saying: «انطلقوا إلى ظل ذي ثلاث شعب، لا ظليل ولا يغني من اللهب» there is a curious art among the arts of rhetoric, which the ancients named «al-ʿunwān» (the title/index). Reference to it has preceded in this book: it consists in the speaker taking up a purpose of his — description, boasting, praise, reproach, satire or other such arts — and then, with the aim of completing it, bringing examples of words that serve as a title for earlier reports and past stories. And there is a very great kind of it, which is what serves as a title for the sciences: that words are mentioned in the speech which serve as keys to sciences and entrances to them. This verse we are dealing with is among the truest proofs of that, for His saying «ظل ذي ثلاث شعب» is a title for the science attributed to Euclid, a Greek philosopher who composed a book on astronomy, geometry and arithmetic, which al-Ḥajjāj ibn Yūsuf al-Kūfī translated into Arabic. He taught geometry in Alexandria in the days of Ptolemy and laid down the principles of plane geometry; he also has the book of the Elements, which Nāṣir al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī commented upon; and he died in the year 283. [Translator's note: translated as written; it is unclear in the source to whom the death date refers, and the details are compressed.] For the triangular figure is the first of figures and their basis, and from it the rest of the figures are composed; and it is a figure which, when set up in the sun, however it is set up and on whichever of its sides, has no shade, because of the sharpness of the vertices of its angles. So Allah, Glorified is He, commanded these people of Hell to go off to the shade of this figure in mockery and derision of them.
4- Simile (tashbīh): He, Glorified is He, likened the sparks to the palace in its hugeness and size, and likened them secondly to yellow camels in form, colour, multitude, succession and speed of movement. We quote here a curious passage of al-Zamakhsharī and then comment on it briefly. He said in al-Kashshāf: «They were likened to palaces and then to camels to make the simile clear; do you not see that they liken camels to al-afdān and al-majādil?» — i.e. palaces, the plural of fadan and mijdal, both meaning palace, as in al-Ṣiḥāḥ. Then he said: «And جمالات was read with ḍamma, which are the thick ropes (qulūs) of bridges; and it is said the ropes of sea ships, the singular being jumāla» — and al-qulūs is the plural of qals, a thick rope among the ropes of ships. Then he said: «And it is said: صفر, intending the genus; and it is said: صفر means black ones tending to yellowness. And in the poetry of ʿImrān ibn Ḥiṭṭān the Khārijite:
دعتهم بأعلى صوتها ورمتهم ... بمثل الجمال الصفر نزاعة للشوى
(It called them with its loudest voice and pelted them with the like of yellow camels, stripping away the scalps.)
And Abū al-ʿAlāʾ said:
حمراء ساطعة الذوائب في الدجى ... ترمي بكل شرارة كطراف
(Red, its locks shining in the darkness, it throws every spark like a leather tent.)
So he likened it to the ṭirāf, which is a tent of leather, in hugeness and redness. It is as though, out of his malice, he intended to go beyond the simile of the Qur'an; and in his conceit at the illusion of surpassing it that he was tempted into, he placed at the beginning of his verse his word «حمراء» as a preparation for it, a proclamation of it, and an alerting of the listeners to its place. But he was blind — may Allah join for him the blindness of both abodes — to His saying, Mighty and Majestic: «كأنه جمالات صفر», for that is equivalent to saying «like a red tent». Moreover, in the simile with the qaṣr, which is the fortress, there is a likening from two aspects: hugeness and height in the air; and in the simile with jumālāt, which are the ropes, there is a likening from three aspects: hugeness, length and yellowness. So may Allah render far his strangeness in his ṭirāf, and the cheeks he puffed out in finding it so original.»
And the author of Nasmat al-Saḥar mentioned, concerning al-Zamakhsharī at His saying, the Exalted:
«إنها ترمي بشرر كالقصر», that he mentioned the verse of Abū al-ʿAlāʾ describing the fire of hospitality, from the qaṣīda rhyming in fāʾ in which he elegized the Naqīb Abū Aḥmad al-Mūsawī, father of al-Sharīf al-Raḍī and al-Murtaḍā, namely:
حمراء ساطعة الذوائب في الدجى ... ترمي بكلّ شرارة كطراف
and he became heated against him and said that he intended and aimed to go beyond the simile of the Mighty Qur'an with the palace. He said: «And I do not know whence he got that he aimed to go beyond the simile of the Qur'an, for it is known that the palace is greater than the ṭirāf, which is a tent of red leather used by the nomadic Turks and the wealthy among the Arabs; but al-Zamakhsharī, despite his merit, was very sharp of temper.»
I say: al-Zamakhsharī — may Allah have mercy on him — picks quarrels with Abū al-ʿAlāʾ in many places, and he is, as we see in his criticism of al-Maʿarrī's beautiful verse, clearly biased and partial. We are accustomed to al-Zamakhsharī attacking the opponents of the Muʿtazila, and Abū al-ʿAlāʾ was not one of them; but al-Zamakhsharī was a man of letters who had read al-Maʿarrī's epistles and took note of his stance toward the grammarians, so his dislike drove him to provoke him.
This grammatical feud did harm to Abū al-ʿAlāʾ, for the grammarians neglected his poetry and very rarely took it up with commentary, citation or criticism; they gave attention to the poetry of Abū Tammām and al-Mutanabbī for their free handling of the language and of grammatical styles, and there was in Abū al-ʿAlāʾ's poetry what would tempt them to study it, but they turned away from it. Al-Maʿarrī's criticism of the grammarians has passed in this book, so renew your acquaintance with it.
As for likening camels to al-afdān, which are palaces, it is very frequent in their poetry. ʿAntara said:
فوقفت فيها ناقتي فكأنها ... فدن لأقضي حاجة المتلوم
(I halted my she-camel there, and she was like a castle, so that I might fulfil the need of one who lingers.)
And al-Maʿarrī was captivated by the description of camels and tried to follow in their footsteps, but he went extremely far into strangeness in that, as in his saying, from a qaṣīda of his in Saqṭ al-Zand addressing the keeper of the House of Knowledge in Baghdad:
وحرف كدال تحت ميم ولم يكن ... براء يؤم الرسم غيره النقط
(And a lean she-camel like a dāl beneath a mīm, and there was no "rāʾ" heading for the trace that the drops had altered.)
The ḥarf is the she-camel, and the dāl is a likening of it; the mīm is the bent-over rider, from the angle of simile, not of lexical explanation; the rāʾī is one who strikes the lung, from raʾāhu when he hits his lung; the rasm is the trace of the abodes, and al-nuqaṭ is rain. We have digressed to this only to set out al-Maʿarrī's strangeness, in criticism of which al-Zamakhsharī did not go beyond the truth.

dervis-irab:35-50.t:
* I'rab:
(هذا يَوْمُ لا يَنْطِقُونَ وَلا يُؤْذَنُ لَهُمْ فَيَعْتَذِرُونَ) A resumed statement, presented to set out the state on that day. هذا is the mubtadaʾ (subject) and يوم its khabar (predicate); the clause لا ينطقون is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. It was also read with a fatḥa on the mīm, being accusative as an adverb, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted predicate of هذا. The wāw is a conjunction; لا is negative; يؤذن is an imperfect verb, passive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir), implied as «it»; لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يؤذن. The fāʾ is a conjunction, and يعتذرون is an imperfect verb conjoined to يؤذن, included in the string of the negation without being caused by it; for this reason it was not made accusative, because had it been made accusative it would inevitably have been caused by it. Al-Samīn's wording: «In the nominative of فيعتذرون there are two aspects. One is that it is resumed, i.e. فهم يعتذرون. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: and the meaning would be that they do not speak with a speech that benefits them, or that they speak at some stations and do not speak at others. The second is that it is conjoined to يؤذن, so it is negated; and had it been made accusative, it would have been caused by it.» Al-Bayḍāwī said: He conjoined يعتذرون to يؤذن to indicate the negation of permission and of excuse-making following it absolutely; had He made it an answer, it would have indicated that their not making excuses is because of the lack of permission, and that would have given the false impression that they have an excuse but were not permitted to give it. (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded. (هذا يَوْمُ الْفَصْلِ جَمَعْناكُمْ وَالْأَوَّلِينَ) The clause is the speech of an omitted saying, i.e. «and it is said to them: this...». هذا is the subject and يوم الفصل its predicate; the clause جمعناكم is explicative, clarifying His saying هذا يوم الفصل, because if it is the Day of Decision between the blessed and the wretched and between the prophets and their nations, then the former and the latter must be gathered so that this decision may take place between them. The wāw is a conjunction or for accompaniment, and الأولين is conjoined to the kāf or is a mafʿūl maʿahu (object of accompaniment). (فَإِنْ كانَ لَكُمْ كَيْدٌ فَكِيدُونِ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; إن is conditional; كان is a deficient past verb; لكم is its fronted predicate and كيد its delayed noun. The fāʾ connects the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) because it is a request clause; كيدون is an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the omission of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the nūn is for protection (al-wiqāya), and the omitted yāʾ of the speaker is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object). (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded. (إِنَّ الْمُتَّقِينَ فِي ظِلالٍ وَعُيُونٍ) A resumed statement, presented to mention the states of the believers concisely after He mentioned the states of the disbelievers at length, so as to complete the balance between this sūra and the sūra before it, namely هل أتى على الإنسان; for in that sūra He mentioned the states of the disbelievers concisely and was lengthy in mentioning the states of the believers. إنّ and its noun; في ظلال is its predicate and عيون is conjoined to ظلال. (وَفَواكِهَ مِمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ) Conjoined to ظلال and عيون; مما is a naʿt (adjective) of فواكه, and the clause يشتهون has no grammatical position because it is a ṣila (relative clause). (كُلُوا وَاشْرَبُوا هَنِيئاً بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ)
The clause is the speech of an omitted saying, and this saying is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of المتقين in the adverbial phrase في ظلال, i.e. they are settled in shades, that being said to them. The parsing of هنيئا has preceded many times, i.e. a ḥāl, i.e. enjoying it wholesomely. بما is attached to هنيئا; the bāʾ is causal and ما is a relative noun; the clause كنتم is the ṣila; كان and its noun, and the clause تعملون its predicate. (إِنَّا كَذلِكَ نَجْزِي الْمُحْسِنِينَ) A causal explanation of the command to eat and drink, i.e. that is Our custom and habit: We reward the doer of good for his good just as We requite the evildoer for his evil. إنّ and its noun; كذلك is a fronted adjective of an omitted maṣdar; the clause نجزي is the predicate of إنّا, and المحسنين is the direct object. (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded. (كُلُوا وَتَمَتَّعُوا قَلِيلًا إِنَّكُمْ مُجْرِمُونَ) The clause is the speech of an omitted saying, and this omitted element is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl of المكذبين, i.e. woe is fixed for them in the state of its being said to them: eat and enjoy yourselves. كلوا is an imperative verb, indeclinable on the omission of the nūn, and تمتعوا is conjoined to it. قليلا is accusative as an adverb of time — a time that does not tarry before it ends with your death and perishing; and in any case, however long it extends and is prolonged, it is little and passing, near and hastening, when measured against the spans of the Hereafter and its long days. The clause إنكم مجرمون is a causal explanation of the threat understood from the command to eat and enjoy a shade that passes, a colour that fades, and a deceptive mirage. إنّ and its noun, and مجرمون its predicate. The wording of al-Kashshāf: «If you say: how is it valid that this be said to them in the Hereafter? I say: it is said to them in the Hereafter as an announcement that in the world they deserved that it be said to them, and that they were worthy of it, as a reminder of their ugly state and of what they brought upon themselves by preferring little enjoyment to everlasting bliss and kingdom. In its manner is the saying:
إخوتي لا تبعدوا أبدا ... وبلى والله قد بعدوا
(My brothers, may you never be far — and yes, by Allah, they have gone far.)
He means: you deserved in your lifetime that this be prayed for you. And He gave as the reason for that their being criminals, as an indication that every criminal has nothing but eating and enjoyment for a few days, then remaining in destruction forever. And it is possible that كلوا وتمتعوا be a resumed statement addressed to the deniers in the world» — i.e. so it would go back to what precedes His saying إن المتقين. Al-Jalāl took this view, and al-Qurṭubī and Abū Ḥayyān supported it. (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded. (وَإِذا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ارْكَعُوا لا يَرْكَعُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction connected with His saying للمكذبين, as if it were said: woe to those who denied and to those who, when it is said to them «bow», ...; or with His saying إنكم مجرمون by way of iltifāt (shift of person), as if it were said: they deserve that it be said to them «eat and enjoy yourselves», then (they are described) by their being criminals and by their being such that when it is said to them «pray», they do not pray. إذا is a future adverb containing the sense of condition; the clause قيل is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; لهم is attached to قيل; the clause اركعوا is the speech of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and the clause لا يركعون has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. (وَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلْمُكَذِّبِينَ) Its parsing has preceded. (فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ بَعْدَهُ يُؤْمِنُونَ) The fāʾ is the faṣīḥa (fāʾ that discloses an omitted condition), i.e. if they do not believe in the Qur'an, then in what thing will they believe? بأي is attached to يؤمنون; حديث is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive of annexation); بعده is an adverb attached to an omitted adjective of حديث; and يؤمنون is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ).

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying: «إن المتقين في ظلال وعيون وفواكه مما يشتهون» there is a majāz mursal (metonymic trope) whose relation is locality (al-maḥalliyya), namely Paradise, because the shades extend, the springs flow and the fruits ripen in it.
2- And in His saying: «وإذا قيل لهم اركعوا» there is also a majāz mursal, whose relation is part-for-whole (al-baʿḍiyya), because He named the prayer by the name of one of its parts, namely bowing (al-rukūʿ). He singled out bowing for mention, although the prayer includes many actions, only because the Arabs used to disdain bowing and prostrating. Muqātil said: it was revealed about Thaqīf; they said to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: relieve us of the prayer, for we do not bend down; it is a disgrace. He refused and said: there is no good in a religion that has no prayer in it — and in a narration: no bowing in it and no prostration.

* Benefits:
The grammarians said: in the like of «ما تأتينا فتحدّثنا» both the accusative and the nominative are permissible in the second verb. The accusative is from two aspects that share the feature that the second differs from the first: one of the two meanings is «you do not come to us talking», and the other aspect is «you do not come to us, so how could you talk to us?». As for the nominative, it is on two aspects. One is that the verb is a partner of the first, entering with it into the negation, as if you said «you do not come to us and you do not talk to us», so they are two negated clauses. The second aspect is that the meaning of ما تأتينا فتحدّثنا is «you do not come to us, yet you talk to us». The Exalted said: هذا يوم لا ينطقون ولا يؤذن لهم فيعتذرون, i.e. so they do not make excuses. And from it is the saying of Jamīl ibn Maʿmar al-ʿUdhrī:
ألم تسأل الربع القواء فينطق ... وهل يخبرنك اليوم بيداء سملق
(Did you not ask the deserted encampment — and it speaks? Yet would a barren, level waste tell you anything today?)
He cut off ينطق from what precedes it and made it nominative as a resumption, i.e. it speaks in any case. Sībawayh said: «He did not make the first the cause of the second, but he made it speak in any case.»
